Google Health demo generator

Technical notes for the synthetic health data used by MTL Explorer demos. Account connection and live Google synchronization are unavailable in demo mode.

The generator requires both mtl.demo-mode=true and mtl.demo-health.enabled=true. Demo deployment templates enable it for every image channel; ordinary installations leave it disabled. On startup it waits for indexing and track calculations, then asynchronously checks the ordinary Health tables and fills missing records. Settings → Processing shows its progress. INFO logs show startup, waiting, missing-day counts, generation batches and completion. Failed batches are retried.

Tracks and the daily overview share one fictional wearable timeline. Overlapping tracks use the same samples; the strongest effort at each timestamp supplies the workload without counting overlapping activity twice. Heart rate follows speed, available elevation and cycling power, with delayed effort response, recovery, daily variation and small correlated fluctuations. Missing elevation means flat terrain. Recording gaps are not filled. Motorized tracks generate modest heart rates and no exercise steps or active calories.

Three mathematical walking, running and cycling GPX routes provide exercise examples. Daily records include steps, distance, active calories, sleep stages, resting heart rate and weight. Daily rollups cover the demo track history and at least the recent period; detailed daily heart rate is generated for the last 90 days by default, with older samples generated along tracks. Samples and raw records identify their synthetic source. No account, tokens or Google synchronization are simulated.

  • Implementation
  • Screenshots

Configuration

mtl.demo-health setting Default Purpose
enabled false Explicit demo-only opt-in
track-percentage 100 Stable selection from 0–100%; approximate below 100%
seed 20261003 Reproducible model and selection
sample-interval-seconds 15 Shared timeline sample spacing, 5–60 seconds
batch-size 25 Maximum days per pass and track IDs per query
recent-days 90 Minimum daily history and detailed sample generation
run-schedule PT1S Delay between active passes

The percentage selects tracks that influence the fictional profile. Shared samples can also match unselected tracks when their timestamps fall within the detailed daily history or overlap a selected track.

Implementation

The Java code lives in googlehealth.demo. It uses the regular GPS and Health tables and the same typed JSON payloads as imported records, so shared Health queries can read generated metrics. It adds no schema, tables or persisted job checkpoints. Existing Health records determine which days need completion; a daily heart-rate summary includes the sample count so missing samples can be detected. Completeness checks group stored sample counts by day once across the requested period. Workloads are combined in memory, with cleaned points loaded one track at a time. Completed days are left alone, and the startup job stops when all required records exist.

Generated metric payloads use the shared HealthMetricPayload Java records and the same per-data-type JSON envelope as imported measurements. The metric reader uses these records too. The demo's missing-sample check reads the nested heartRate.sampleCount field.

Health queries and calculations have no generator dependency. Screen labels use the general demo status. Configuration changes affect newly filled records; recreate the demo database to regenerate a complete dataset with new settings.
